steps.name: TF activity: decoupler ulm on CollecTRI
caveats: A prior knowledge network is tissue-agnostic: a kidney-specific regulator absent from the network is missed, and targets silent in kidney add noise. State this.
An activity score is an inference from a curated network, not a measurement — a high score is a hypothesis about a regulator for follow-up, not a demonstrated driver

steps.context: Aldosterone acts through the mineralocorticoid receptor NR3C2, a ligand-activated transcription factor whose activity can change with no change in its own transcript level. The analysis must therefore report inferred activity independently of the TF's own expression, and it should state explicitly where NR3C2 and the glucocorticoid receptor NR3C1 (which shares response elements) fall in the ranking, whether or not they reach significance. A regulatory network cannot be inferred de novo from 12 samples, so a prior network is the only defensible source of regulons here.

steps.description: Infer TF activity with decoupler's univariate linear model on a signed human TF-target regulon network, run two ways. (1) Contrast-level: score every TF on the Wald statistic of ALL tested genes from T1S2, giving one activity estimate and p-value per TF for aldosterone vs vehicle. (2) Per-sample: score every TF on the per-sample log2 CPM matrix from T1S1, then test the resulting score matrix between the two conditions with a moderated linear model (design ~condition, vehicle as reference) and adjust across regulators with Benjamini-Hochberg. Keep the sign of each edge so a repressed target lowers rather than raises the score, and test only TFs with at least 5 targets among the tested genes. Repeat the whole inference with a second, confidence-filtered TF regulon resource (levels A-C) as a concordance check, and report the overlap and the disagreement among the top regulators of the two networks. plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney: TF activity inference
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question is which transcription factors drive the aldosterone-treated kidney samples relative to vehicle controls, on a 12,000 gene x 12 sample raw Salmon count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) with a single condition column in metadata.csv (6 aldosterone vs 6 vehicle, unpaired, single batch, human). TF activity from bulk RNA-seq is an inference from a prior regulatory network, not a measurement, so the plan is built to give that inference two independent, well-conditioned inputs and to state its limits.

T1S1 establishes sample structure before any model: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap and library sizes, so an outlier or a depth artefact is seen before it is interpreted as regulation. T1S2 does the minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size) and fits the PyDESeq2 Wald model with vehicle as the explicit reference level, contrast condition: aldosterone vs vehicle, apeglm LFC shrinkage for reporting, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering and a p-value histogram diagnostic. Its purpose here is not a gene list for its own sake but the per-gene Wald statistic that the contrast-level TF inference consumes, ranked over every tested gene rather than a thresholded subset.

T2S1 is the answer step. decoupler's univariate linear model runs twice on the CollecTRI human signed regulons (the reference store holds CollecTRI 2.0 as CSV): once on the Wald statistic of all tested genes to give one activity score per TF for the aldosterone-vs-vehicle contrast, and once on the per-sample log2 CPM matrix to give a score per sample per TF, which is then tested between the two groups with a moderated linear model and BH across regulators. The two views must agree in sign for a TF to be reported as a driver. DoRothEA (confidence A-C, also in the store) runs as a second network for a concordance check, since a regulon-derived activity that flips with the network is not a finding. A regulatory network cannot be inferred from 12 samples, so a prior network is the only sound source here and no expression-derived network is attempted.

T2S2 puts the TF result in signalling context with the PROGENy footprint model (decoupler mlm, top 500 responsive genes per pathway) on the same contrast statistic, read as a footprint rather than pathway membership, and annotates the leading TFs with their own differential expression — a TF's activity and its own transcript level often diverge, and saying so prevents overclaiming. T1S3 assembles the report with the required provenance: network name and version, input statistic, contrast, estimator, minimum regulon size, number of regulators tested, the explicit caution that an activity score is a hypothesis about a regulator, and a full reproducibility record.

All scripts are Python per the user constraint; PyDESeq2 and decoupler (2.2.0) are both installed, so nothing falls back to R. The mineralocorticoid receptor NR3C2 itself is a ligand-activated TF whose activity can change with no change in its own transcript — the analysis must be able to detect that case and report it, not read NR3C2 mRNA as its activity.

steps.name: Pathway footprint context and TF annotation
steps.question: Which signalling pathway footprints accompany the TF activity changes in aldosterone-treated kidney, and how do the leading TFs' own expression levels compare with their inferred activity?
steps.description: Run decoupler's multivariate linear model on the PROGENy human footprint model over the aldosterone-vs-vehicle contrast statistic from T1S2, using the top 500 responsive genes per pathway, to give a pathway footprint score with p-value per pathway. Also compute per-sample pathway scores on the log2 CPM matrix and compare between groups. Separately, for the leading TFs from T2S1, join their own differential expression result from T1S2 (log2FC, padj, baseMean) beside their inferred activity, and state for each whether its own transcript changed. Reference data needed: the PROGENy human footprint model of pathway-responsive genes with weights; if it is not resolvable in this environment, report the TF result without the pathway footprint layer and say so — the research question is answered by T2S1 and does not depend on this step.
steps.context: Pathway footprints are read as the transcriptional consequence of pathway activity, not as expression of pathway members. This step is interpretive context for the TF result, plus the TF-expression-versus-TF-activity comparison that keeps the report honest about mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: Pathway footprint table for the aldosterone-vs-vehicle contrast: score, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value per pathway
Per-sample pathway score matrix with the between-group comparison
Leading TFs from T2S1 annotated with their own log2FC, padj and baseMean from T1S2, and an explicit note of whether activity and own-expression agree
Interpretation states footprint, not membership, and names the model version
If the footprint model is unavailable, the step reports that fact and still delivers the TF-expression annotation
constraints: Python only
pathway_activity: activity_method = mlm
pathway_activity: top_responsive_genes = 500
pathway_activity: interpretation = footprint, not membership
Do not claim pathway topology impact — no topology-aware method is available here
caveats: A pathway member can change expression with no change in pathway activity, and the reverse — the footprint score is the claim, member expression is not
This step is context, not the answer: if the footprint model is absent the run still answers the research question from T2S1

grounding.reason: PROGENy footprint with decoupler mlm on the contrast statistic, top 500 responsive genes (R-0115); SPIA is absent so no topology claim is made (R-0122).

steps.name: Consolidated report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which TFs drive the aldosterone response in kidney', with its provenance and its limits stated?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S2, T2S1 and T2S2. Lead with the ranked TF activity result for the aldosterone-vs-vehicle contrast, giving for each reported TF: the activity estimate, adjusted p-value, number of targets used, whether the contrast-level and per-sample analyses agree, whether the second regulon network agrees, and the TF's own differential expression. State the network name and version, the input statistic, the named contrast, the estimator, the minimum regulon size, and the number of regulators tested. State plainly that an activity score is an inference from a prior network and not a measurement. Include the DE summary (genes tested, genes significant by direction, p-value histogram shape, NA attribution) and the QC outcome. Close with a reproducibility record: package versions, random seeds, the regulon collection version, and session info. Where the evidence is weak — few targets, network disagreement, contrast/per-sample disagreement — say so in the same sentence as the finding.
steps.context: Twelve samples and a prior-knowledge network set a hard ceiling on what can be claimed. The report's job is to make the strength of each TF call visible rather than to produce a clean ranked list that reads as more certain than it is.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked TF table with estimate, adjusted p-value, target count, cross-view agreement, cross-network agreement, and own-expression, in one place
Network name and version, input statistic, contrast (condition: aldosterone vs vehicle), estimator, min regulon size, and number of regulators tested all stated
Explicit statement that activity scores are network-derived inferences and are hypotheses for follow-up
DE and QC summaries included, with the p-value histogram shape and the NA attribution
Reproducibility record present: package versions, seeds, regulon collection version, session info
No TF is presented as a confirmed driver on the basis of the activity score alone
constraints: Python only
report: state network_name, network_version, input_statistic, contrast, estimator, min_regulon_size, n_regulators_tested, inference_caution
report: reproducibility record covering session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version
caveats: Do not upgrade a TF activity hypothesis into a mechanistic claim; no perturbation or binding data is present in this dataset to support one

grounding.reason: Activity report fields and reproducibility record per R-0119 and R-0086.
